`_expanded` maps onto `SongDetailCard.IsPresenting`, and that only flips to false when the collapse *animation* lands (see SongCardMotion.CollapseLanded / SongDetailCard.Advance). During a collapsing animation `_expanded` stays true while the card is already shrinking toward row height. Consequences in this file:

1. `ApplySearchFilter()` invoked every frame by `StepCardAnimations` keeps the old row hidden until the landing frame — intended — but anything that reads `_expanded` in that window (e.g. `IsCurrentPreviewLoad` in Loading.cs, `EnsureSelectedRowVisible`) still believes a full card is presented.
2. In the `_visibleOrder.Count == 0` branch the code calls `CollapseCard()` and then `ApplyEmptySelection()`, which calls `_detailCard.ShowEmpty()`. With motion enabled the card is still presenting/shrinking, so the empty text/card overlays the shrinking list until the animation lands.
3. `OnRowPressed` early-returns via the `_expanded && index == _packIdx` branch, so pressing the (invisible) selected row while collapsing re-requests a collapse instead of expanding.

Consider tracking an explicit page-level `_cardExpanding`/`_cardCollapsing` state instead of deriving it from the presentation flag, so click handling and empty-selection logic don't depend on animation timing.
comments.existing_code: private bool _expanded => _detailCard.IsPresenting;

comments.content:
`ApplySearchFilter()` now mutates selection and calls `BeginRefreshAll()` (which calls `CallDeferred(CompleteRefreshAll)` and touches `_rows[i].Selected`, `_libTitle`, `_detailCard.*`). It is invoked from several re-entrant paths:
- `ExpandCard()` (line 81), right after `_browse.SelectPack(index)` + `ClearPreload`. If the newly selected pack does not match the current query, this block immediately selects `_visibleOrder[0]`, so the user pressed row B but row A gets selected and the card is expanded at `_rows[_packIdx]` (now A) — the expand target silently differs from the pressed row.
- `_detailCard.Advance(..., ApplySearchFilter)` on the collapse landing frame — inside the Godot animation step, so a second refresh can be scheduled while a previous `CompleteRefreshAll` is still queued.
- `TextChanged` on every keystroke, meaning a deferred full chart refresh per keystroke that cancels the selection.

Additionally the calls are not guarded by `_localTransitionBusy || TransitionDirector.IsBusy`, unlike `OnRowPressed`/`BrowseNextDifficulty`.

Recommend separating “filter rows” (pure visibility/empty-state update) from “selection repair + refresh” so `ExpandCard` and the animation callback don't trigger an unexpected re-selection/refresh.

This unconditionally overwrites the empty-state text. `BuildLibrary()` installs a different message for the empty-catalog case ("曲库为空：把谱面包放进 …"), and `ApplySearchFilter()` is called right after `BuildLibrary()` in `_Ready` (SongSelect.cs line 52), so that guidance is immediately replaced by "没有匹配的谱面". Operators end up seeing "no matching charts" when the library is genuinely empty and never see where to put packs. Compute the text based on `_browse` catalog size (`GameSession.Packs.Count == 0` / no rows) rather than always overwriting.

The row hit-test maps a content-Y back to the *visible-index* position, assuming the rendered rows are tightly packed with stride `RowHeight + RowGap`. That assumption breaks in two cases:
- While a card is expanded/collapsing, an unoccupied hole of height `RowHeight + RowGap` exists at the card's slot (`_detailCard` sits inside `_rowBox` and takes `max(RowHeight, ShownHeight)` + one separation). Clicks in that hole or below it resolve to the wrong pack.
- The trailing `_emptyState` label and any hidden rows obviously don't participate; but `withinRow > RowHeight` also rejects the gap. Note `withinRow` can never be negative given the FloorToInt math, so the `withinRow < 0` check is dead code.

If the intent is to ignore the inter-row gap, the boundary should be checked against actual row geometry (or the check relaxed to `>= RowHeight` semantics) instead of a dead negative branch. Consider using the row control's global rect for the hit test so expanded-card offsets can't mis-select.

The Esc handler keys on `Keycode` only. For non-Latin layouts / IME input, Esc arrives with `Keycode == Key.None` and the physical key in `PhysicalKeycode`, so the handler is skipped and the event falls through — leaving focus in the search box. Match on `PhysicalKeycode` (or `Keycode == Key.Escape || PhysicalKeycode == Key.Escape`).

Setting `_search.Text = ""` fires `TextChanged`, which already runs `ApplySearchFilter()` (Layout.cs line 192); the explicit `ApplySearchFilter()` here is redundant and makes the filter/selection-repair logic run twice, potentially scheduling two `BeginRefreshAll` refreshes. Drop the explicit call and rely on the signal, or set text with the signal temporarily muted.

The guard only validates `_packIdx` once at the top, but `ApplySearchFilter()` on line 81 can re-select a *different* pack (`_visibleOrder[0]`), and `_rowBox.MoveChild(_detailCard, _rows[_packIdx].GetIndex())` then runs against the re-selected index. `_rows` is populated from `GameSession.Packs` at build time while `_browse` uses its own catalog snapshot, so after `ApplySearchFilter` these can point at different entries (and, if `_rows` were ever rebuilt/reordered, `_rows[_packIdx]` could throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`). Capture the resolved row/index after the filter call and re-validate before `MoveChild`, or assert `_rows.Count == browse catalog count` at construction.

`OnRowPressed` already calls `CallDeferred(nameof(EnsureSelectedRowVisible))` and then `BeginRefreshAll()`, while `ExpandCard` queues another deferred `EnsureSelectedRowVisible`. Each press thus queues two deferred scroll-to-visible calls in the same frame. Harmless visually but pointless work and noise when debugging; `OnRowPressed` should not queue its own call when it always goes through `ExpandCard`.
comments.existing_code: CallDeferred(nameof(EnsureSelectedRowVisible));

comments.content: `_handoff` is only constructed in `_Ready()`, but both `Configure()` and the `Coverage` setter dereference it unconditionally (only the setter has an `IsInstanceValid` guard). `TrackHandoffPresentation.Configure` also writes `_relayHeading`/`_relayStatus`/`_cover`, which are built in that child's `_Ready`, and `Coverage` calls `UpdateContentVisibility()` on a self-null-guarded label set. This works today only because `TransitionDirector` adds the child to the tree and awaits `IsNodeReady()` before `Configure`; any other caller (tests, tools, re-parenting, deferred configure) would NRE or silently write to null. Add an explicit readiness guard, e.g. ensure the handoff is lazily created (`_handoff ??= EnsureHandoff()`) and make `Configure` defer if not inside the tree yet, instead of relying on a null-forgiving field.

`Configure` writes to `_label`/`_detail`/`_handoff` with no readiness check, while `UpdateContentVisibility` (called right below) does have a null guard — the class is internally inconsistent about whether these are usable pre-`_Ready`. Also `_handoff.Configure` internally calls `_state.Reset()`, so a mid-transition reconfigure does reset the handoff phase, but `Coverage` on the handoff is re-applied while the overlay's own `_kind`/`_waitingScan` are reset; make the pre-ready behavior explicit rather than relying on field-level `!= null` checks.

In the Back direction the slice rects are never clamped to the design area: with `_coverage` near 0 the edge is 1920 and `offsets[i] * direction` yields +78, so slices are drawn at x=1998 / 2088 / 2094 with width 116, i.e. entirely off-screen. The positive direction is clamped with `Mathf.Max(0f, ...)` but the negative direction has no equivalent clamp on the right side. Clamp `sliceEdge` into `[0, DesignWidth - 116]` for both branches.
comments.suggestion_code:
var sliceEdge = Mathf.Clamp(edge + offsets[i] * direction, 0f, UiLayout.DesignWidth - 116f);
            var rect = new Rect2(sliceEdge, y, 116f, h);

comments.content: `_waitingScan` can advance to (near) 1f and `Mathf.Lerp(100f, 1820f, 1f)` returns the exact end value, so the scan line settles at x=1820 which is fine; but the `>= 0.999f` check is duplicated in `DrawSignalSlices`, `DrawCutEdge` and `DrawScan` with the same magic constant and the loop/waiting branch condition in `DrawScan` is `_coverage >= 0.999f && _profile.AllowLoop` while `DrawCutEdge`/`DrawSignalSlices` bail out purely on coverage — meaning in a looped waiting state the cut edge and slices are *not* drawn but the scan moves independently, and once the scan has moved off the edge the composition looks broken. Extract a single `IsFullyCovered` property and keep the geometry consistent between the three draw calls.

`AdvanceWaitingScan` clamps only the divisor and ignores the sign/size of `delta`. `TransitionDirector` advances phases with frame deltas, but after a long hitch, a debugger pause, or a paused SceneTree resume the first `_Process` delta can be large; the scan then jumps arbitrarily. More importantly, the phase can also be re-entered (`AwaitingSceneReady`) while `_waitingScan` keeps its previous value, since nothing resets it except `Configure`. Clamp delta (e.g. `Mathf.Clamp(delta, 0f, MaxSeconds)`) and reset `_waitingScan` when entering the waiting phase, or fold the scan animation into `TrackHandoffState` which already handles reset consistently.
comments.existing_code:
var loop = Math.Max(0.01, _profile.LoopDuration);
        _waitingScan = Mathf.PosMod(_waitingScan + (float)(delta / loop), 1f);

comments.content: `DrawSignalMarks` is copied verbatim from `TrackHandoffPresentation.DrawSignalMarks` (same positions, same alpha ramp). Duplicated drawing code will drift the moment one of them is tweaked (and in fact the two `DefaultLabel`/`DefaultDetail` helpers below are also duplicated with slightly different wording mappings). Move the shared mark geometry into a small static draw helper and have both call sites use it.

`DefaultDetail(TransitionKind.Gameplay)` returns "SYNCING PLAYFIELD" here while `TrackHandoffPresentation.DefaultDetail` returns the same for Gameplay but the two switch expressions duplicate the whole table. Since the overlay's label/detail is hidden for Gameplay/Restart (only the handoff child renders text for those kinds), the `Gameplay`/`Restart` arms of these helpers are dead for the overlay's own labels; keeping them invites divergence. Either delegate to a single shared source of default copy or drop the unreachable arms.

`DefaultLabel`/`DefaultDetail` aside, `DrawSignalSlices` allocates a new `float[] { -78f, 0f, 66f }` array on every `_Draw` call (i.e. every frame during a transition). Hoist it to a `private static readonly float[] SliceOffsets` like the other static tables in this file, and mark `DrawSignalMarks`'s signature unused `direction` parameter accordingly.
comments.suggestion_code: // field: private static readonly float[] SliceOffsets = [-78f, 0f, 66f];
comments.existing_code: var offsets = new[] { -78f, 0f, 66f };

comments.content: `_overlay.MarkFailed()` is only meaningful when a Track Handoff presentation is active. In `Standard`/`Back` transitions (the majority of routes — Settings, SongSelect, Main), the overlay is a plain cover; calling `MarkFailed` flips the handoff state even though no handoff was ever started, which may leave the handoff presentation in a failed state that later `ClearPresentation` was not designed for. Also, this branch is only reached while still fully covered, so a "failed" visual is never actually visible to the player. Guard it with `IsTrackHandoff` or drop the call.

The timeout recovery path does not clear the pending reveal callbacks from the scene that timed out (`_revealProgress`/`_revealCompleted` remain whatever the failed scene set, if anything). More importantly, if the timed-out scene *did* call `ReportSceneReady` late (after the 15s window) it will be ignored because `_sceneReady` was reset to false and `_phase` stays `AwaitingSceneReady` — but if the same scene instance was replaced by the recovery route this is fine. The actionable issue is that `_sceneReady` is not explicitly reset here (it is false already in this branch, but relying on that invariant is fragile); reset it together with `_lockElapsed = 0.0`, since a stale `_lockElapsed` from a scene that briefly reported ready before timing out would let the recovery scene's hold gate pass instantly. Recommend resetting `_sceneReady = false; _lockElapsed = 0.0;` alongside `_phaseElapsed = 0.0;`.

`AcceptSceneReady` reads the deferred `TryBeginRevealDeferred` path but the reveal *also* starts directly in `AdvanceWait`. `TryBeginRevealDeferred` can fire after the phase already moved to `Revealing`/`ReadyBarrier`; it guards on `_phase == AwaitingSceneReady`, so that is safe. However, when there is no pending navigation, `ReportSceneReady` invokes the progress callback with `1f` and then the completion callback synchronously, while `_revealProgress`/`_revealCompleted` are never stored — fine. The real risk: `AdvanceWait` calls `BeginReveal()` on the same condition as `TryBeginRevealDeferred`, so on a paused-tree frame both may run in the same frame (deferred call is flushed before/after `_Process` depending on ordering). `BeginReveal` guards on `_phase`, so this is currently safe, but it duplicates the reveal-start condition in two places; consider extracting a single `TryBeginReveal()` used by both so the gating logic cannot drift.

Input suppression is incomplete. `_Input` only marks events as handled *after* they were already dispatched to `_Input` handlers registered earlier (tree order of the autoload) and does nothing for `_ShortcutInput`, `_UnhandledKeyInput`, or `Control` nodes that use `ProcessModeEnum.Always` and consume events in `_GuiInput` (which runs before `_Input` is finished for GUI members). During a transition a UI node with `Always` processing can still react to clicks/keys — e.g. a second `Navigate` while covering, or gameplay input that resumes while the incoming scene is already in the tree but not yet revealed. Consider also intercepting `_ShortcutInput`/`_UnhandledKeyInput` and/or setting `GetViewport().GuiDisableInput = true` (or `SetInputAsHandled` at the earliest autoload position) while busy.

The `CanvasLayer` added in `_Ready` is never freed or detached, and `_Layer`/`_overlay` are reassigned on every `_Ready`. That is fine for a single autoload instance, but combined with the duplicate-instance guard in `_EnterTree` (which calls `QueueFree()` on the duplicate) the duplicate is removed during tree entry and `_Ready` never runs — acceptable. Still, `_Ready` creates the overlay without anchors/offsets; if `UiLayout.DesignSize` differs from the actual viewport at runtime (window resize, non-16:9), the overlay may not cover the whole screen. Prefer `SetAnchorsAndOffsetsPreset(LayoutPreset.FullRect)` so the cover always matches the viewport, or derive the size from `GetViewport().GetVisibleRect()` on resize.

`AdvanceOpaqueBarrier` increments `_opaqueFrames` on every `_Process` tick regardless of whether the frame was actually rendered, and it relies on `_Process` running while `SceneTree.Paused = true` (it does, since `ProcessMode = Always`). But `_opaqueFrames` is `int` and never reset if `SwitchScene` fails and `RecoverToCurrentScene` completes with the non-animated path; the field is only reset on the next `BeginNavigation`. That is fine. The more subtle bug: the barrier counts process ticks, not rendered frames, so with a very high process rate vs. render rate (or `Engine.MaxPhysicsSteps`-style catch-up) the scene switch may still occur before the opaque overlay is visible. `RenderingServer.FramePostDraw` (one-shot deferred via `CallDeferred(nameof(...))` inside `RenderingServer.Singleton.FramePostDraw`) or `RenderingServer.RequestFrameDrawnCallback` would be the correct primitive for 'at least one fully opaque rendered frame'.

`RecoverToCurrentScene` (called when `_beforeSwitch` throws or `ChangeSceneToFile` fails) sets `_phase = Revealing` but does not reset `_lockElapsed`/`_opaqueFrames`; more importantly, if the failure happened in `SwitchScene` *after* `_phase = AwaitingSceneReady` was set and the scene change failed, the `_route` still holds the failed route and `_kind` indicates a Track Handoff — `AdvanceReveal` then calls `_overlay.AdvanceHandoff(delta)` and `RevealHoldDuration()` may wait for `DischargeSeconds` (0.5s) even though no handoff was begun (`BeginHandoffReveal` was never called because `BeginReveal` was bypassed). This makes the recovery reveal hold on a discharge animation that was never started. Clear the handoff state (e.g. call `_overlay.ClearPresentation()` or reset `_kind = TransitionKind.Standard`) before switching to `Revealing` in the recovery path.

`_profile` is captured once at navigation start; if the player changes the motion mode on the Settings screen, the transition that returns to Main/SongSelect still uses the old profile. This is a minor UX inconsistency, but the larger concern is the code path: `GameSession.Settings.MotionMode` is read on the main thread here — ensure `Navigate`/`BeginNavigation` is never invoked from a background thread (e.g. an audio/thread-pool callback in `GameSession`), because `ChangeSceneToFile`, `GetTree().Paused` and `CallDeferred` must run on the main thread. Nothing in the file asserts main-thread affinity; consider documenting it or guarding with `OS.GetThreadCallerId() == OS.GetMainThreadId()`.
comments.existing_code: _profile = UiMotionProfile.For(GameSession.Settings.MotionMode);

comments.content: `_treeWasPaused` is stored on the instance (not per-navigation) and is restored only in `CompleteTransition`. There are no early `return`s from `_Process` paths that skip `CompleteTransition`, so this holds today. But the pause is set *before* `_overlay.Configure`, so if `Configure` (overlay reconstruction / relay presentation) throws, the exception escapes `BeginNavigation` after the tree was paused and after `_phase` is still Idle — `Navigate` returns without unwinding, leaving the tree paused with no transition running, which is a permanent soft-lock (input handlers are not suppressing because phase is Idle, but the game is frozen). Wrap the overlay configuration in a try/catch that restores `GetTree().Paused = _treeWasPaused` and resets to Idle on failure, or set the pause only after `Configure` succeeds.
comments.existing_code:
_treeWasPaused = GetTree().Paused;
        GetTree().Paused = true;

comments.content: Ctrl+S can never be reached while a LineEdit has focus because of the earlier `GuiGetFocusOwner() is LineEdit` guard, and it also runs after the `!_flowPage == Edit` gating. More importantly, the `if (!key.Pressed) return;` line is placed *after* the Z/X handlers but before Ctrl+S — that's fine — however the Ctrl+S branch sits after the LineEdit early-return, so saving from the editor is impossible whenever any text field is focused. If saving is meant to be globally available (the comment only exempts canvas commands), move the save branch above the LineEdit guard.
comments.existing_code:
if (!key.Pressed) return;
        if (key.Keycode == Key.S && key.CtrlPressed) { RequestSave(key.ShiftPressed); return; }

comments.content: Regressions/ambiguities in the shortcut chain: (1) The `S`/`W` audio-rate branch (`Key.S or Key.W`) below is dead for the S key unless Ctrl is held? No — Ctrl+S returns above, bare `S` never reaches it because... actually it does, but `Ctrl+S` is consumed first only when Ctrl is pressed. However, bare `S` conflicts with nothing — still, note that `SetAuto(!_playing)` uses `_playing` while F1 uses `_auto`; since `SetAuto` sets both, they can diverge when playback is stopped by other paths (e.g. `ReturnToPack` sets `_playing = false` without changing `_auto`, and `ShowFlowPage` also sets `_playing = false`). After returning from Pack to Edit, `_auto` is still true while `_playing` is false, so Space and F1 toggle in opposite directions and the HUD AUTO indicator desyncs from actual playback. Use a single source of truth (always `_auto`) here.

        if (key.Keycode == Key.F1) { SetAuto(!_auto); return; }

comments.content: Invariant gap: when `_timeTarget` is already at a clamp boundary (0 or Duration), `_timeTarget` does not change, so the `_timeTarget + seconds` value is clamped back to the same value; then with inertia enabled `_time` will keep easing toward an unchanged target — that's fine — but if `_time` has overshot the (possibly shrunk) `DurationSeconds`, no clamp is applied to `_time` here. If the document is reloaded with a shorter duration while inertia is mid-flight, `_time`/`_timeTarget` can stay beyond `DurationSeconds`. Consider clamping `_time` and `_timeTarget` to the current duration at the start of this method.

_timeTarget = Math.Clamp(_timeTarget + seconds, 0d, _canvas.DurationSeconds);
        if (EditorSettings.Current.ScrollInertiaTauSeconds <= 0d) JumpTime(_timeTarget);

The same pattern appears in the `M` and `R` keyboard handlers and in the reverse case `ActPlayFromMark`/`ActReplay` (and `Space`/`F1` via `SetAuto(!_playing)`). After starting playback from the menu, the HUD still shows AUTO off while audio/notes are running. Route every playback start through `SetAuto(true)` to keep `_playing` and `_auto` in lockstep.

comments.content: While the context menu is open, *every* mouse motion event anywhere in the window is swallowed (`SetInputAsHandled`) even when the pointer is far from the menu. This blocks hover/scroll and any other input consumer (HUD buttons, page controls) for the lifetime of the menu — and the menu can stay visible indefinitely. Forward the event to the menu only when `_menu.ContainsGlobalPoint(motion.Position)`, and don't mark it handled otherwise.

The wheel handler above correctly requires `_flowPage == EditorFlowPage.Edit` and a canvas hit, but there is no equivalent guard for the menu. If the page changes to Settings/Create while the menu is somehow still visible, subsequent clicks/motions are consumed globally before the page can see them. Consider also closing/hiding the menu when the flow page changes, or gating this block on `_canvas.Visible`.

comments.content: `Directory.Exists` / `File.Exists` on arbitrary external paths run on the main thread for every drop; also, only `files[0]` is inspected, so a multi-file drop silently ignores the rest without any feedback. More importantly, non-existent paths (e.g. a broken shortcut target) are reported with the misleading "Start 页只收目录" message. Report the actual reason when the path exists as neither a file nor a directory.

Snapshot inconsistency: `state.NodeMode` and the `NODE` header come from `SingleSelection`, but `state.Header` is only populated when a single selection exists. When `HasSelection` is true with a multi-selection (`SelectionCount > 1`), `SingleSelection` is null and the menu falls back to the generic panel — which is intentional per the comment — but `state.StepsEnabled` stays false even though `StepSelection` acts on the whole selection. Confirm `StepsEnabled` should really be disabled for multi-selection; otherwise steppers appear greyed out while the operations would work.

`_side` is assigned but never read to drive anything in this file except the numeric tool-key branch (`if (_side == 3)`), while `_canvas.SetSide(...)` calls go through `_canvas` directly. In particular `_canvas.CurrentSide` is the authoritative value in `BuildMenuState`, so `_side` can drift from the canvas (e.g. `_canvas.SetSide` called by other paths). Either drop `_side` and query `_canvas.CurrentSide`, or ensure every side mutation updates both consistently.

`_lastPlayableSide` is written in `SetPlayableSide` but never read anywhere in the file; when the user switches to side 3 (free/path) via the numeric keys / context menu (`_side = 3; _canvas.SetSide(3)`), the remembered playable side is never used to restore. This is dead state — either use it to restore on `Up`/side toggles or remove it.

if (key.Keycode == Key.Z) { _canvas.TimeSnapOverride = !key.Pressed; return; }
        if (key.Keycode == Key.X) { _canvas.SpaceSnapOverride = !key.Pressed; return; }

comments.content:
Like DrawGridLines, this loop is bounded only by `bar <= lastBar`. The grid loop guards itself with `i - first <= 10000`, but here nothing caps the iteration count. With a degenerate document (very short BPM interval making `EditorTime.SecondsToBar` explode, or an extreme DurationSeconds) `lastBar` can be enormous and this tight loop runs thousands/millions of times every `_Draw` (which fires per frame while anything redraws). Apply the same iteration cap used in DrawGridLines.

Also note `lastSecond` uses `CursorTime + SidePreviewTravelPx / PixelsPerSecond` while `DrawGridLines` uses the same upper bound but the lower bound `49d` magic constant is duplicated in both methods — extract a shared helper so the two cannot drift.
comments.suggestion_code:
var guard = 0L;
		for (var bar = firstBar / step * step; bar <= lastBar && guard++ <= 10000; bar += step)

comments.content: `VisibilityAlpha` returns 0 for a hidden track, and the grid loop skips drawing lines for that side — but `DrawBarNumbers`, `DrawBpmEvents`, `DrawBarRuler`, `DrawProgressLine` and (most importantly) `DrawSelectionOverlay` do not consult `_trackVisibility` at all. So hiding the center track (or a side track) hides the grid but still shows bar numbers, the BPM line, the selection outline and path handles for notes on that track. That is inconsistent with the visible "track OFF" state and lets the user edit/hit shapes they cannot see. Either gate the per-track overlays on `VisibilityAlpha(side) > 0f` or document why those layers intentionally ignore track visibility.

Ghost ids are derived from the runtime note `Id`, which is assigned as `headId = _gameplayNotes.Count + 1` (see `AppendGameplayNote`/`BuildRuntimeChain`). Because the ghost (or hover ghost) is appended last, its ids are typically `Count+1 .. Count+n`. If a real note in the chart happens to carry the same numeric id, the ghost id set will collide and real notes will be rendered as ghosts (or the ghost will be suppressed from the ghost styling). Ids for the real chain are regenerated sequentially every refresh rather than read from `note.Id`, so stability is not guaranteed. Consider using a dedicated sentinel id range far outside the sequential range (e.g. negative ids) for drafts/hover ghosts so collisions are structurally impossible.

`_gameplayStage` is null-checked at the top of the method and returns early, so this is safe — but `SetGhostNoteIds`, `SetNotes` and `SetPreviewTime` are called unconditionally on it after the loop. If a future refactor removes the null guard this NREs; more importantly, `RefreshGameplayStage` is invoked from `_Process` on every dirty frame, meaning `SetNotes` re-allocates/re-uploads the whole note list each frame during a drag (`_stageDirty` is set on every pointer move). Consider only rebuilding/re-pushing when the note set actually changed (hover ghost position changes every pointer move, so at least avoid rebuilding the full real-note chains each time — cache the non-draft prefix and only rebuild the appended ghost segment).

In path-edit mode `DrawSelectionHandle` draws the head outline here, while `DrawPathHandles` also draws a head diamond handle for the same note (`HeadHandleCenter` / `InDiamond(HeadHandleCenter(note), ...)` in `AuthoringCanvasPath`). That means the head is signalled twice (rectangle outline + diamond) and — more importantly for a multi-selection — every other selected note's `Nodes` handles are drawn on top of the currently edited note in the same frame, making the path-edit target hard to distinguish. Verify against the design intent that the head outline should be skipped when `pathEdit` is true.

`ApplySize` has no null / validity guard: a caller passing a `null` Control (e.g. an optional field that was never built) throws NullReferenceException, and passing an already freed/queued-for-deletion Control calls `AddThemeFontSizeOverride` on a disposed GodotObject (ObjectDisposedException / native crash). Since every control in the editor funnels through this single entry point, add an early-out that mirrors the checks already used in `TryGet` (respect the `!` nullability contract, but still defend the freed-node case).

`ApplySize` both prunes dead entries and appends a new one, while `ReapplySizes` can run from the settings callback (EditorFlow.Settings.cs). If a control is (re)created during the same frame the scale is replayed, the two paths mutate the shared static `Registered` list without any synchronization or re-entrancy guard. A `ReapplySizes` invocation re-entered from inside `AddThemeFontSizeOverride`/`QueueRedraw` (or any future call from a worker thread) can corrupt the list or cause an index-out-of-range on the backward loop. Consider documenting/enforcing main-thread-only usage (e.g. `Debug.Assert` on the main thread) or taking a snapshot (`Registered.ToArray()`) in `ReapplySizes` so mutation during iteration is safe.

The registry only ever grows during a session: dead entries are pruned lazily and only when `ApplySize`/`ReapplySizes` runs. In a long editing session that builds/destroys many pages, `Registered` keeps accumulating `SizeEntry` objects (each holding a `WeakReference`) until the next scale change. Since callers are not asked to unregister, consider exposing an `Unregister(Control)` helper (or pruning on `TreeExited`) so the list stays bounded.
comments.existing_code: private static readonly List<SizeEntry> Registered = new();

comments.content: `TryGet` validates the control, but `AddThemeFontSizeOverride` is still called on a node that may become invalid between the check and the call only in a multi-threaded scenario — more importantly, `Control` can legitimately be a tree-less/orphan node and this is fine, but the call is not wrapped in any validity re-check. Given `TryGet` already revalidates, consider an `if (!GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(control)) continue;` immediately before the override to make the intent explicit and guard against races with `QueueFree` processing. Low severity given the current single-threaded usage.

Bug in the new-key path: the hovered key is seeded with a single step (e.g. 1.0f with a 60fps delta) but `unsettled` is unconditionally set to true, and the seeded value is never re-targeted in the same call. Concretely:
- The seeded value may already equal the target (delta >= Seconds, or the first frame after a frame spike), yet `unsettled` stays true → the page keeps `_Process(true)` running forever, since on the next frame the key exists in `_values` with value == target, the loop sets no `unsettled`, and the key is not expired... so it does terminate on the next frame — but that is an extra idle frame and, worse, contradicts the documented contract "返回 true 表示还没全部到终值".
- Conversely, when a *newly hovered* key is seeded while `off == false` and `delta` is tiny, the value is fine, but the seeding bypasses `MoveToward`; the semantic is inconsistent with the loop branch.
- Also, if `hoveredKey` was just expired in the loop above (e.g. hover moved back to a key whose value had already reached 0 within this same call), the key is deleted and then immediately re-inserted from 0, which is correct, but only because removal happens before insertion — this implicit ordering dependence should be made explicit.

Fix: seed the key in the main loop or set `unsettled = _values[hoveredKey] != 1f` after seeding (and for the off path leave it false).

Two issues with the expiry logic in the enumeration:
1. Writing `_values[key] = next` inside a `foreach` over `_values` is only safe because assigning to an *existing* key does not bump the Dictionary's version. That is fragile and easy to break by a future refactor (e.g. switching to a remove-then-add or a `TryAdd`). It also silently relies on the deferred-removal list — worth a comment or, better, collecting a snapshot of keys and mutating afterwards.
2. The `next <= 0f` check is used for removal, while `MoveToward` with target 0 lands exactly on 0 so this is currently fine. However, for a key that is *not* hovered and *not* yet at 0, `unsettled` is set correctly; but for a key that is the current `hoveredKey` with `value == 0` (MOTION OFF at value already 1 from a previous cycle) nothing is expired — fine. The real gap: if `off` is true and a stale key's target is 0 while its stored value is 0 (cannot normally happen because 0 entries are deleted), no drift exists — OK. Still, comparing with `next == 0f` (or `next <= 0f` plus a tolerance) should be documented as relying on MoveToward's exact landing.

MOTION-OFF semantics: when `off` is true and the previously hovered key was already at 1, the loop snaps it to 0, removes it, and inserts the new hovered key at 1 — the return value then depends solely on the new-key branch. That is acceptable, but note `off` is read once per call while the single-element `HoverFade.Update` reads it per call as well, so toggling the setting mid-transition (`HoverFade` value 0.5, motion turned off) will snap on the next frame — consistent. The inconsistency is only the spurious `unsettled` described above: with MOTION OFF the method should always be able to return false in a single frame (it currently returns true for one extra frame whenever a new hovered key appears, causing `_Process` to stay on for a frame that cannot change anything). Also consider guarding `delta <= 0` to avoid re-running the loop with zero progress while `unsettled` stays true.

`HoverFade.Seconds` is a `const float` but `Seconds` is also the field name — `HoverMotion.Seconds` is fine, yet `(float)delta / HoverMotion.Seconds` divides by a constant that could be zero if someone edits it; a `Mathf.Max` guard is cheap insurance. More importantly, `_value != target` uses exact float comparison: with `MoveToward` this terminates because the step is clamped to the remaining distance, but if `delta` is large enough that the step exceeds the distance, MoveToward already clamps — so it's fine. No change strictly needed; flagging only the unchecked zero divisor.
comments.suggestion_code: : Mathf.MoveToward(_value, target, (float)delta / Mathf.Max(HoverMotion.Seconds, 0.0001f));

comments.content:
`BpmAt` is fragile and disagrees with `EditorTime.SecondsToBar` at boundary events. Two problems:

1. Seeding `resolved = bpms[0].Time` and using `entry.Time >= resolved` as a monotonic guard relies on `CurrentBpms` being sorted by `ExactBarTime`; `EditorTime` defensively re-orders (`OrderBy(item => item.Time)`), but this loop does not. If the list is ever unsorted (e.g. a BPM moved to a later time by a command path that doesn't sort, or a hand-built chart), the first element can be skipped and the wrong BPM reported for BAR/BPM in the HUD and for grid density.
2. At an exact boundary (cursor bar == event.Time) `SecondsToBar` still returns the *previous* segment's BPM in some rounding cases, whereas `BpmAt` returns the new one; BAR and BPM can then be computed with different BPMs. `BarSecondsAt` compounds this because it only uses the instantaneous BPM.

Resolve the active BPM through the same ordered timeline used by `BarToSeconds` (walk the ordered list and keep the last entry with `Time <= bar`), or derive it from `BarToSeconds(prevBar)/BarToSeconds(bar)` so both agree.

`SnapTime` snaps in bar space with `EditorTime.SnapSeconds` and then converts back with `BarToSeconds`. For a snapped bar that falls beyond `DurationSeconds` (e.g. cursor in the last partial grid cell) the conversion can overshoot and is then hard-clamped to `DurationSeconds` — a non-grid time. `MinimumHoldDuration` uses `GridStepSecondsAt(t)` computed at the *current* time, so at a BPM boundary the minimum hold may not match a single grid step from the snapped start time, allowing a hold tail that snaps back onto its own head (zero-length hold) or that requires two grid steps. Compute the minimum duration as `BarToSeconds(bar + 1/GridDivisor) - BarToSeconds(bar)` starting from the *snapped* hold start bar, and reject/advance the tail when the resulting end bar is not strictly greater than the head bar.
comments.existing_code: private double MinimumHoldDuration(double t) => SnapEnabled ? GridStepSecondsAt(t) : .04;

comments.content: The fine path (`fine == true`) has no upper bound: holding Ctrl/Cmd+V repeatedly grows `GridDivisor` unbounded. Every grid/redraw path then iterates `GridDivisor` subdivisions per bar (`SecondsToBar` per bar in `_Draw`, plus per-frame grid drawing), so an unbounded divisor is both a UI lock-up risk and makes the projection math meaningless. Clamp the fine path to a sane maximum (the coarse ladder tops out at 64).

Decreasing from a non-ladder value strictly below 32 produces a *smaller* divisor than it should: e.g. `current == 31` (set via the fine path) hits the `_ => Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Floor(current / 32d) * 32)` branch, which floors to `0` and clamps to `1` — a jump from 1/31 to 1/1 instead of stepping down to 24. The same branch makes the ladder non-monotonic relative to the `current <= 8` branch. Prefer flooring to the previous ladder rung (e.g. 24 for 31, 16 for any value in (16,24]) rather than `Math.Floor(x/32)*32`.
comments.existing_code: _ => Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Floor(current / 32d) * 32),

comments.content: `DurationSeconds` is a public settable property with no validation, and `_cursorTime` clamping depends entirely on it. Setting it to `0`, a negative value or `double.NaN` (e.g. a transient projection state) makes `Clamp(v, 0, max)` return the invalid max (`Math.Min(max, Math.Max(min, v))` with `max < min` yields `max`), which then flows into `EditorTime.SecondsToBar`, `AxisAt` and `RemainingPx` and throws (`SecondsToBar` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for non-finite input). Guard the setter (`Math.Max(0d, value)` and reject non-finite) so a bad document duration can't crash the canvas.
comments.existing_code: public double DurationSeconds { get; set; } = DefaultDurationSeconds;

comments.content: `TotalBars()` calls `EditorTime.SecondsToBar(DurationSeconds, ...)` without guarding finiteness, while the rest of the canvas carefully clamps. If `DurationSeconds` was assigned a non-finite/invalid value this throws during `_Draw`, crashing every frame. Guard with `double.IsFinite` and fall back to 1 bar (mirroring `AuthoringCanvasSelection` which already guards this).

private int TotalBars() => Math.Max(1,
		(int)Math.Ceiling(EditorTime.SecondsToBar(DurationSeconds, CurrentBpms).ToDouble()));

comments.content: `SelectedEventIndex` and `SelectEvent`/`TryEvent` compare BPM events by exact `ExactBarTime` equality over the projection list. `BpmAt`/`ExactTimeAt`/`SnapTime` round-trip seconds → bar → seconds, so after a BPM edit the projection times may differ in the last rational digit from the value produced by `SnapSeconds`, making `FindIndex(item => item.TimeExact == time)` silently return -1 and the BPM selection unreachable (Delete/SelectedSummary then do nothing). Consider matching by key/id or by nearest-time tolerance instead of exact equality.

comments.content: `Undo`/`Redo` call into the controller without any exception isolation, unlike `DeleteSelection` which wraps `DeleteBpm`. A document command that throws (e.g. inconsistent state after `SyncFromDocument` restored a stale selection, or a BPM command hitting a missing base event) will propagate out of the input handler and leave `SyncFromDocument` unexecuted, desynchronising the projection from the document. Either make the controller's undo/redo non-throwing or guard them like `DeleteSelection` does.

`CancelInteraction` only restores from the document when a `_gesture` is present. A `_draft` in progress mutates `_projection` (the ghost/placement preview writes into the projected note list) without a gesture; cancelling the draft clears `_draft` but never calls `SyncFromDocument`, so any provisional note the draft pushed into the projection persists visually until the next unrelated sync. Either make drafts not mutate `_projection`, or restore the projection unconditionally (`_draft is not null || _gesture is not null`).

Also, a backdrop created later (e.g. by `BuildCommunityStageChrome` reloads) will never be dimmed. Consider caching the backdrop nodes after build and re-applying only to those.

comments.content:
`delta` is not validated. Both callers feed the engine's per-frame delta, which can be <= 0 in edge cases (first frame, a paused/stopped frame, or a large clamped spike):
- `delta == 0` → exponent 0 → next == current, fine but the caller keeps `_Process` on forever.
- `delta < 0` → `1 - e^(+|delta|/tau)` yields a factor < 0, so `next` moves *away* from `target` (divergence, oscillation).
- A very large `delta` makes `-delta/tau` a huge negative number; `Math.Exp` then underflows to 0 and the result is fine, but if `target - current` is huge while `delta/tau` is huge, the smoothing becomes a jump — acceptable — however a NaN/Inf in `delta` or `tau` propagates to `next` and the snap check `Math.Abs(target - next) <= TimeSnapSeconds` becomes `false` for NaN, leaving the view permanently non-converged (infinite repaint).
Guard against non-positive/non-finite `delta` and non-finite `tau`: treat them as the instantaneous path (return `target`) so the caller always converges.

The float overload has the same `delta`/`tau` robustness gap as the double one (negative delta → moves away from target; NaN/Inf delta → NaN result → `Math.Abs` NaN → snap never triggers → `StepScroll` returns true forever and `_Process` never stops, i.e. permanent redraw). Note the caller `PackPageOverlay.StepScroll` only exits when `_scroll == _scrollTarget` exactly, so a NaN would wedge the process loop permanently. Apply the same guards and additionally snap on non-finite `next`.

`PixelSnap = .5f` is applied to a scroll offset expressed in pixels, but the wrap distance also depends on `tau`: with very small `tau` (slider near left but > 0) each step is a near-full jump, which is fine; the issue is the opposite — the snap threshold is a fixed absolute distance, so for a scroll region the visible row height (row pitch) can be smaller than 0.5 px at high zoom-out, meaning the caller may stop up to half a row short of the intended offset and the last partial row never gets drawn fully. Consider documenting/deriving the threshold from the row pitch or lowering it; at minimum, the constant's doc should state it's in the same units as `current`/`target` (pixels/screen units, possibly scaled by canvas zoom).
comments.existing_code: public const float PixelSnap = .5f;

comments.content: Missing `<summary>`/`<param>` docs for a public static API used from two pages; more importantly, the tolerance semantics differ between overloads (absolute time seconds vs. absolute pixels) while both are named `Step` and share the same parameter list. A caller passing a time-based `delta` with a view-space `current` (or vice versa) type-checks fine. Consider renaming to `StepSeconds`/`StepPixels` (or adding `[Obsolete]`-style doc warnings) so misuse is visible at the call site.

comments.content: `Load()` relies solely on `file.GetAsText()`. If the file exists but `FileAccess.Open` returns null (e.g. the file was deleted/rotated between `FileExists` and `Open`, or permission denied), `file.GetAsText()` throws `NullReferenceException`. That is caught, but it also means a genuinely unreadable file is reported only as a warning and silently replaced with defaults; worse, `Open` failure leaves no explicit check, so the root cause is obscured. Guard for a null handle and log a clear reason.

            var data = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<SettingsData>(file.GetAsText());

comments.content: The catch block calls `ResetToDefaults()` after some fields may already have been assigned inside the try block, and `Load()` starts with `ResetToDefaults()` too. If deserialization succeeds partially (fields assigned one by one before an exception, e.g. an `InvalidOperationException` on a malformed number of a later property — or any exception thrown by `ParseMotionMode`/assignments), the catch restores defaults, which is correct-but-lossy: all previously valid fields from the file are dropped. More importantly, `JsonSerializer.Deserialize` here uses default options, so a single malformed value (e.g. `"snapStep": "abc"`) throws and discards every other valid persisted setting. Consider deserializing into a tolerant structure (per-field reads via `JsonDocument`/`JsonElement.TryGet*`) so one bad field does not wipe unrelated settings, or at minimum document/test this all-or-nothing behavior.

`GridChoiceIndex` / `SnapChoiceIndex` / `UiScaleChoiceIndex` use `Math.Max(0, Array.IndexOf(...))`. `IndexOf` returns -1 when the value is not an exact element of the array. `ClampValues()` normally snaps values onto the arrays, but `Load()` calls `ClampValues()`, so this should hold — except when `Save()`/`Load()` are not the only writers: any code assigning `DefaultGridDivisor`/`SnapStep`/`UiScalePercent` directly (they are public setters) can leave a value like `12` or `0.15`, and the index expression silently maps that to 0 while the value itself stays mismatched — the UI stepper then shows the wrong selection and stepping from index 0 overwrites the user's value. Either make the setters private (route all writes through a clamp method) or derive the index from `Nearest(...)` instead of `IndexOf`.

`ParseMotionMode` falls back to `Full` for any unrecognized string (including typos like `"reduced "` or `"REDUCED"`), and `Capture.ClampValues()` does not recompute anything for enum values because `Full` is valid. So corrupt persisted `motionMode` strings are silently swallowed with no warning, contradicting the file's own design goal of not “disguising dead values as persisted settings”. Emit a `GD.PushWarning` when the raw string is non-null but unmatched, so bad files are diagnosable.

`Save()` swallows all write failures with only a warning, and the in-memory state stays diverged from disk with no signal to callers. If callers assume a successful save (e.g. showing “saved” / not re-prompting on exit), user settings are silently lost. Consider returning `bool` (or exposing a `LastSaveFailed` flag) so the settings page can surface the failure — the atomic `SettingsFilePersistence.Write` throwing is exactly the case worth reporting.

`Nearest` ties bias toward the first/lowest choice because of the strict `<`. For values with no exact midpoint (e.g. grid divisor `24.5`), the result is deterministic, which favors the lower tier. Please add unit tests covering: midpoint ties (grid `12` → 8 or 16?), whitespace/unknown motion strings, out-of-range values from an old file (e.g. `uiScalePercent: 150` → 125, `backgroundDimPercent: 100` → clamped only by `ClampValues`, not by `Nearest`), NaN in `snapStep`, and the `GridChoiceIndex == -1` fallback.

`TimeSpan.FromSeconds` throws `OverflowException` for magnitudes beyond `TimeSpan.MaxValue` (~9.2e11 seconds), and a `NaN`/`Infinity` input from an upstream cursor computation (e.g. division by zero tempo) will fall through `Math.Max` unclamped. Since this is called every HUD refresh (`EditorHudView`), a single bad value would crash the editor loop instead of showing a placeholder. Guard for finiteness and clamp to a sane upper bound.

        TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Math.Max(0d, seconds)).ToString(@"mm\:ss\.fff", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

Derive the rule from the page width (anchor left=right or update `Size.X` on resize) or reuse a shared design-width constant so it stays aligned across resolutions.

comments.content: The theme-color overrides are keyed by raw strings in a loop over a locally-allocated array (allocated on every button creation). `"font_hover_color"` is not a valid `Button` theme color (`Button` uses `font_*_color` keys but the hover/pressed text colors live under `font_hover_color`/`font_pressed_color` only for `Label`-like controls — `Button` does use them, however `font_focus_color` does not exist for `Button`), so an invalid key is silently ignored and provides no protection. More importantly, `EditCutButton._Draw` already draws the text-state colors itself, making these overrides redundant. If they are intentionally kept, replace the stringly-typed names with `Button` theme constants/`ThemeConstants` and avoid the per-call array allocation.

`LevelTagText` only checks `Level is null`, so a chart with `Unrated == false` and `Level == 0` renders `· LV 0`. If 0 is used as the "unset" sentinel in `EditableChart` (common when level is stored as a plain int after deserialization), that leaks an invalid rating badge into the HUD. Confirm the sentinel contract; if 0 means unset, treat `Level <= 0` as the placeholder.

`DifficultyName` uppercases the enum name for the built-in branch but passes `chart.DifficultyKey` through verbatim for `Custom`, so a custom key stored as lowercase would render inconsistently next to the uppercased built-in names. Also falls back to `"CUSTOM"` for null/empty keys; an empty string (not just null) would produce a blank label. Normalize both branches the same way and treat empty keys as missing.

These formatting/utility helpers (`DifficultyName`, `LevelTagText`, `CursorTimeText`) are pure functions with non-trivial edge cases (negative/NaN seconds, null level, custom difficulty keys) but have no test coverage found in the repo. Add unit tests for the boundary cases.

comments.content: `SpaceSnapOverride` is documented (AuthoringCanvas.cs:74-77) as "sets these false while a key is held" and defaults to `true`. So `fine = !SpaceSnapOverride` makes the *coarse* step the default and the fine step the modifier — matching `Place`/`HandleButtonMotion` (`SnapCenter(value, SpaceSnapOverride ...)`), so the inverted-looking expression is actually consistent. The real problem is that the code is easy to misread as a bug and that `SpaceSnapOverride` is meant as a temporary pointer-modifier flag: if a menu command is invoked while the modifier is stuck (e.g. key-release event lost when focus changes, or the menu is opened with the X key held), the step size silently changes. Consider renaming to a dedicated `SpaceFineOverride`-style property or at least a local `bool fine = SpaceSnapOverride;` with a comment, so intent is explicit.

comments.content: `_controller.StepSelection` can throw: `RequireNote`/`RequirePathNode` throw `KeyNotFoundException` when the snapshot's `NoteId`/`NodeId` no longer exist (CanvasAuthoringController.cs:103-106), and `StepTime` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `gridDivisor <= 0`. `SingleSelection` is derived from the last projection, so if the document was mutated elsewhere (undo/redo via a different path, external sync) the snapshot can be stale and this menu command will crash the editor instead of emitting a status line. Same for `SetPathNodeCurve`, `SetHoldJudge` and `DeletePathNode` below (none of the three can throw a *recoverable* error caught here; `DeletePathNode` can throw `InvalidOperationException`/`KeyNotFoundException`). Wrap the controller call in try/catch and emit a rejection status, like `DeleteSelection` does for `DeleteBpm`.

`var updated = SingleSelection ?? target;` can never fall back in practice: in `SyncFromDocument` the projection is rebuilt and `_selection.Restore(Notes, BpmEvents)` is applied, so if the note was removed the selection is dropped and `SingleSelection` is null — reading `updated.NodeTime`/`NodeCenter`/`NodeWidth` then falls back to the *pre-step* snapshot, which is fine, but if the selection became multi-selection it would also silently print a stale value. More importantly `EditorStepProperty.Time` for a *note* (not node) target reports `ExactBarTimeText.Format(updated.NodeTime)`, and `SelectedTarget.NodeTime` is `node?.TimeExact ?? note.TimeExact`, so this is correct — but it is confusing that the readout of a note uses the `Node*` fields while `CENTER`/`WIDTH` use `NodeCenter`/`NodeWidth` too. Consider exposing `Time`/`Center`/`Width` on `SelectedTarget` (resolved once) and using those here instead of duplicating the `IsNode ? ... : ...` selection logic in three places (snapshot ctor, chip text, status text).
comments.existing_code:
SyncFromDocument();
        var updated = SingleSelection ?? target;

comments.content: Two issues: (1) `target.IsTail` is computed from the stale snapshot — `IsTail => NodeIndex == NodeCount - 1`, but `NodeIndex` is `-1` when `nodeId` was not found in `SingleSelection`, which would misclassify. Here it is guarded by `target?.NodeId is null`, so index >= 0; still, `IsTail` is `true` when `NodeCount == 1` mathematically, harmless. (2) The order is `_selection.SelectNote(...)` then `SyncFromDocument()`: `SyncFromDocument` calls `_selection.Restore(Notes, BpmEvents)`, so the manual `SelectNote` is redundant at best; worse, if `DeletePathNode` throws (tail/validation failure in `EditorCommandRules.ValidateNote`) the selection has not been touched but `SyncFromDocument` is never called, leaving the canvas showing the deleted node. Wrap `DeletePathNode` in try/catch, set the selection only after success, and drop the redundant pre-sync `SelectNote`.

The chip is only clamped to >= 0, never to `DesignWidth`/`DesignHeight`, and only the X > DesignWidth overflow is considered (the `Math.Max(0f, x)` clamp can place the chip back *over* the note when the note is near the left edge). Since the chip's own hit test (`HandleChipPress`) consumes presses inside `layout.Chip`, a chip pushed partially outside the stage or on top of the selected note will block selecting/dragging that note. Also `Notes` can contain notes whose `NoteRect` is drawn off the authoring area; the chip would then be pinned at (0,0). Clamp both axes against `DesignWidth - ChipWidth` / `DesignHeight - ChipHeight` and keep the chip clear of the note rect.

`HandleChipPress` swallows both press *and* release on the chip, but the canvas gesture state machine (`_gesture`, `_draft`, `_selection.MarqueeActive`) is bypassed here. If a press began on a note (before `ChipLayout()` returned a chip, e.g. the chip appears mid-drag), the release inside the chip rect is consumed here and `EndPrimary` never runs, leaving `_gesture` dangling. Conversely a press that starts on the chip returns `true` without starting anything, while a release on the chip after a drag started elsewhere is also swallowed. Restrict the swallowing to `pressed` (and handle the release only when a chip press was actually started, tracked via a `_chipPressActive` flag).

`FindNote` is called from `ChipLayout()`, which runs on every `_Draw` and on every mouse-motion event (`UpdateChipHover`), performing a linear scan of all notes. On dense charts this is an O(n) scan at input rate. Either cache the selected note when the projection is rebuilt in `SyncFromDocument`, or use the note index already resolved by `FirstSelectedNote()` inside `SingleSelection` (expose it on `SelectedTarget`) instead of re-searching by id.

Hold commit can throw and leave the canvas stuck. `MaximumCenter - Width` semantics aside, the real problem is that `MinimumHoldDuration(d.Time)` is a *grid step* (up to a whole grid interval) while `DurationSeconds` may be shorter than one step: `Math.Max(0, DurationSeconds - MinimumHoldDuration(t))` is clamped at 0, so a hold dropped at/near the end of the chart is placed at t (line 148-149), and at commit `d.Time + MinimumHoldDuration(d.Time)` is clamped by `UpdateTail` to `DurationSeconds` -> `tail == time`. `CanvasAuthoringController.AddNote` then throws `InvalidOperationException("Path tail must be strictly after the head.")` (CanvasAuthoringController.cs:39-40). That exception escapes `_Input` and `_draft` is never cleared, so the draft overlay sticks until Escape. If the user starts a chain draft (`_tool == 2`) and then releases without a hold path, `_tool` is re-armed from the committed kind — fine — but if `_tool` changes between begin and end (e.g. a shell shortcut in `StandaloneEditorMain` that calls a tool setter while a draft is live), the draft must be cancelled or the tool setter must refuse while `_draft/_gesture` are active. Currently there is no guard, so tool changes mid-draft silently change what the next commit produces. Consider centralizing 'tool change requires CancelInteraction()' here.

`HandleMotion` recomputes/changes hover state even during an active marquee or drag, and the pointer-leave/out-of-area branches do not finalize anything. Concretely: when the pointer leaves the authoring area while `_selection.MarqueeActive`, the marquee keeps the last point but no redraw/end happens — acceptable — yet when the pointer leaves while a draft is in `TailStage`, `_pointerInside` goes false but the draft stays live indefinitely with no visible cancel path other than Escape. comments.content: `FinishGesture` treats `gesture.Moved == false` as 'nothing changed' and discards the drag, but `UpdateGesture` already mutated the projection before returning false from `Advance(...)`? No — `Advance` is checked first, so projection mutation only happens once `Moved` is true; however, if `Advance` returned true and the preview rejected the move (`MoveNodeTime` returned null) the projection is unchanged yet `Moved` is true, and `FinishGesture` will still call `gesture.Commit` with the *original* (unmodified) values. That is mostly harmless (controller no-ops when values are equal), but it calls `SyncFromDocument()` and `QueueRedraw()` on every such drag end. Also, if `Commit` throws (e.g. `KeyNotFoundException` when the node was deleted concurrently), `_gesture` is already nulled but `SyncFromDocument` is skipped — wrap the commit in try/finally.

`AddBpmEvent` duplicate detection is inconsistent: it first searches `BpmEvents` with a 1e-4 seconds tolerance, then re-checks the document with exact `item.Time == exact` equality. Because `SnapTime(time)` and `ExactTimeAt(t)` apply different snap paths, a BPM that exists at the same grid position can fail both checks (tolerance mismatch in seconds vs exact bar comparison) and `AddBpm` will throw or create a duplicate BPM at the same exact time. Use the single authoritative exact value: resolve `exact = ExactTimeAt(time)` first and check `BpmEvents.Any(x => x.TimeExact == exact)`.

`AddBpmEvent` looks up the newly inserted event with `BpmEvents.FindIndex(item => item.TimeExact == exact)` after `SyncFromDocument()`. If the projection stores a *different* exact value (e.g. `SnapSeconds` produced a non-canonical fraction that the document normalizes), FindIndex returns -1 and `SelectEvent(-1)` silently *clears* the selection instead of selecting the new event. Guard the index, and prefer returning the index/id from the controller.

Conversely, on sides 1/2 clicking a BPM label falls into the generic branch and begins a marquee instead. Either remove the dead branch or hoist the BPM hit test above the `_side == 3` split so BPM events are editable from any track view.

The doc comment says the tail-stage visual is the dashed path preview, and the head is no longer a ghost, so this cross-hair may be unintended/stale. The alpha ramp never reaches zero: the outermost segment is drawn at `TimeGuideAlpha * 1 / steps` (~9%), so the fade ends on a visible hard line rather than fading out, and alpha is stepped (banding) while each frame issues ~41 antialiased `DrawLine` calls that run every tick during a gesture. Drawing the two ramps as a single gradient polyline (or gradient texture quad) would remove both the banding/edge step and the per-frame draw-call overhead.

Error handling in ConfirmCreate is misleading for AddDifficulty: `AddChart` may have already mutated the document (the chart is appended via `AddChartCommand`), so when the subsequent `ShowFlowPage(...)`/refresh path throws, the user sees "创建失败：…" although the chart was really added. Retrying then hits a "Chart ID already exists" error and the user may conclude nothing was created. In addition, `SetFlowMessage` only writes to the Create overlay while `_flowPage == Create`; `ShowFlowPage(Pack)` sets `_flowPage = Pack` *before* `RefreshPackPage()`, so an exception thrown during the refresh is reported to the Pack page with the generic "创建失败" text even though creation succeeded. Any previously reported save error would remain in the HUD until the next save/refresh, and the ordering (clearing the error before showing the page) is subtly load-bearing. comments.content: `result.DraftRequest!` and `result.Chart!` are force-unwrapped based on `_createMode`, but nothing ties `_createMode` to what `EditorCreateRequest.Build` returned. If the mode and payload ever disagree (e.g. a future mode value or a refactor of `Build`), the user gets a raw NullReferenceException wrapped as "创建失败：Object reference not set…" instead of a meaningful message. Add an explicit guard that turns a mode/payload mismatch into a clear InvalidOperationException.

Duplicate chart ID and duplicate custom difficulty key are re-checked only here (ID) and, for the difficulty key, not re-checked at all beyond the preflight snapshot built earlier. `ConfirmCreate` calls `CoreCreateForm`/`Build` but does not re-run `EditorCreatePreflight.Validate` against the live document. If the document changes between prefill/preflight and confirm, the ID check catches collisions but the custom-key duplicate check is skipped, producing two charts with the same folded custom key. Re-running `EditorCreatePreflight.Validate` (or moving the duplicate checks into the session/command layer) before mutating would close this gap.

Preflight only checks audio/cover availability in the `NewPackage` branch (`newPackage && File.Exists(...)`). For AddDifficulty the flags are always false, and `EditorCreatePreflight.Validate` ignores them in that branch anyway. The harm is the reverse direction: for NewPackage, `File.Exists` is evaluated eagerly regardless of mode, and `File.Exists` silently returns false for permission-denied/locked paths, so the user gets "音频文件不存在或不可访问" with no distinction. The eager `File.Exists` calls are also duplicated work on every validation keystroke (called via the overlay `Validate` hook), i.e. disk I/O in a keystroke path. Consider short-circuiting per mode and caching/limiting the file probes.

`NextChartId` probes "chart-{i:00}" in a loop from 1 with an O(n) `Any` scan per candidate, i.e. O(n²) over the chart count and O(n) string allocations per pass. The numeric format also breaks past 99 charts (`chart-100` still formats as `chart-100`, but the zero-padded assumption makes IDs inconsistent) and ignores non-standard IDs. A single pass collecting existing IDs into a `HashSet<string>` (Ordinal) and scanning upward once would be simpler and linear.

The tolerance must mirror the snap actually applied, i.e. `!SnapEnabled ? (small epsilon) : (SpaceSnapOverride ? SnapStep : FineCenterSnap) * .5d`. (The `carrying` branch ignoring position/width entirely is intentional per the doc, but the same SnapEnabled gap applies to it if it ever starts classifying.)

comments.content:
`BuildPackSnapshot()` is called once per `TryDigest()`, and `TryDigest` is called from `RefreshPackPage`, i.e. on every Pack-page repaint. `Charts.Single(...)` also throws (or `BuildPackSnapshot` may fail on an invalid document) when the selected chart id is not present, and the enclosing catch then reports "digest unavailable". Two issues:
1) Performance: the whole pack snapshot is rebuilt just to get one `JudgePreset`; and this happens on every repaint.
2) Correctness/diagnostics: a missing selected chart (a genuine state bug) is silently indistinguishable from "hash pending" / "no audio".
Prefer looking up the preset from the selected chart directly (e.g. `_document.SelectedChart` / a cheap accessor) and handle the not-found case explicitly.

The blanket `catch (Exception)` collapses every distinct failure mode (invalid chart failing `V2SemanticValidator.ValidateChart`, invalid preset `Tutorial`, bad hex, missing chart id, unexpected bugs) into `false`. Callers only render a dimmed `DIGEST —`, so real defects/regressions in digest computation are invisible during development. Consider at least distinguishing `ArgumentException` (expected: chart currently not valid) from unexpected exceptions (log them via `GD.PushWarning`/`PushError` so they surface) instead of swallowing everything.

Re-dispatch path: the task just cleared `_digestPending` and set `_digestExpectedPath = null`, then calls `EnsureDigestAudioHash(path)`. Inside, the metadata key is recomputed; if the file is still being rewritten the key will keep changing, and each completion re-dispatches — potentially looping indefinitely while a slow writer keeps touching the file, and each iteration reads the whole file on a background thread. There is no attempt counter / backoff.
Also, when the result is dropped because `path != ResolveDigestAudio()` (line ~119), nothing clears `_digestAudioMetaKey`, leaving stale meta state; the next `EnsureDigestAudioHash` will correctly recompute it, but the state is inconsistent with the "pending cleared" invariant. Recommend bounding retries (e.g. max N attempts, or record the failed meta key and don't retry until it changes again) and resetting `_digestAudioMetaKey` when dropping the result.

Meta key uses (last write time UTC, length). Two `FileInfo`/`File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc` stat calls are made (one for time, one for length via the fresh `FileInfo`), and `FileInfo` caches its data at first access — mixing a static call and a `FileInfo` instance can return inconsistent values for the same file. Use a single `FileInfo`/`File.GetAttributes`-free stat (e.g. `var info = new FileInfo(audio); info.Refresh(); return $"{info.LastWriteTimeUtc:O}|{info.Length}";`).
Note too that FS timestamp granularity (1s on some filesystems) means a same-length, same-second content replacement cannot be detected — this is a caveat worth documenting rather than a race the current code can close.

`File.ReadAllBytes` loads the entire audio file into a managed array just to hash it, and it also copies it again in `SHA256.HashData` semantics on the stream. For large audio files this allocates a large buffer per attempt (and retries from `ApplyDigestAudioSha` can repeat it). Prefer streaming: `using var stream = File.OpenRead(path); return SHA256.HashData(stream);` which avoids the full-file allocation and works on arbitrarily large files.

`InvalidateDigestAudioHash` clears `_digestPending`/`_digestExpectedPath` but does not bump any generation counter. Combined with `ApplyDigestAudioSha`'s guard, a scenario still slips through: if invalidation happens after the background task finishes but before the deferred callback runs, then a *new* `EnsureDigestAudioHash` for the same path is dispatched by `TryDigest`, and the old callback (same `path`, `_digestPending == true` again) will be accepted — writing the hash computed from the *previous* file content. The meta re-check mitigates this only when the file changed on disk; for save/invalidate without file change nothing guards it. A monotonically increasing `_digestGeneration` captured at dispatch and compared in the callback would make the guard unambiguous.
Also note `Task.Run` is fire-and-forget: exceptions from `CallDeferred` after node free are lost, and there's no way to observe the failure. At minimum keep a reference to the task or use `ContinueWith` with error logging.

When a task is already in flight for the *same* path but the metadata key has changed (file replaced), this early-returns and waits for the in-flight task. The in-flight task's own meta re-check will then detect the mismatch and re-dispatch, so correctness holds — but worth noting the `_digestAudioMetaKey = metaKey` below this early-return never runs in that case, so `_digestAudioMetaKey` keeps the old in-flight key until the callback. That's intentional (the callback compares against it), but it is easy to break; documenting the invariant "_digestAudioMetaKey always holds the meta key the currently in-flight/last completed task was dispatched with" would help future edits. No change required if intentional.

`_auto` and `_playing` are treated as equivalent only inside SetAuto, but the rest of the flow diverges: `_playing = true` is set directly on M/R key jumps (StandaloneEditorMain.cs:302/312) while `_auto` stays unchanged, and ShowFlowPage sets `_playing = false` without touching `_auto`. Consequently the Space branch (`SetAuto(!_playing)`) vs F1 branch (`SetAuto(!_auto)`) can flip into different states, and the HUD keeps showing "AUTO" while playback is actually stopped (or vice versa). Either keep both flags strictly synchronized at every assignment site, or derive the HUD flag from `_playing` rather than a separate `_auto` field.

SetAuto does not refresh the HUD despite the doc comment stating the GRID/SNAP row (which renders the `AUTO` suffix, see EditorHudView.Refresh) is refreshed by this method. Toggling auto via Space/F1 therefore leaves the HUD's AUTO indicator stale until some other code path happens to call RefreshEditHud (the only caller today is OpenChart). Add a RefreshEditHud() call here, or correct the comment.

`_hudView` is declared as non-nullable with `= null!`, so the `?.` in RefreshEditHud silences the compiler but does not really handle an uninitialized HUD: if RefreshEditHud is ever reached before BuildEditChrome (during InitializeEditorFlow ordering changes), the HUD silently keeps stale values instead of failing loudly. Since BuildEditChrome is called unconditionally from InitializeEditorFlow, drop the `?.` (and the `null!` initializer) so misuse fails fast instead of silently skipping the refresh.

`CurrentDir` is only assigned when `PackageDirectory` is non-null; when saving an in-memory draft for the first time (or when a previous save dialog left a stale directory) the dialog reopens at whatever location it was last left in, which can be a deleted directory or an unrelated folder. `InvalidateDigestAudioHash()` is only invoked on the success path. `V2PackageWriter.Write/Create` can write audio/cover bytes to the destination and then fail during publication cleanup (as the catch comment itself acknowledges), but the digest cache still points at the previous audio file. The next `TryDigest()` then reports a hash computed from a file that no longer matches what is on disk, giving a misleading "valid" digest. Move the invalidation into a `finally` block (or invalidate at the start of the save) so cached state is never stale after a partial write.

Catching every `Exception` here swallows non-recoverable errors (e.g. `OutOfMemoryException`, `StackOverflowException` cannot be caught, but `OperationCanceledException`, `ArgumentException` from programmer error, etc.) and reduces them to a UI string with no diagnostic trace. Debugging a save failure will be very hard because nothing is logged. Log the full exception (and stack) before reporting, and consider rethrowing or at least distinguishing expected IO/validation failures from unexpected ones so they are not silently hidden from telemetry.

The save result is order-sensitive by design: `RefreshPackPage()` calls `SetPackStatus(...)`, which resets the status line, so the result must be written afterwards. This implicit coupling is fragile — a future change that makes `RefreshPackPage` (or the HUD refresh inside `ReportSave`) push its own message will silently drop the "SAVED/CREATED" feedback. Extract the refresh-then-report into a named helper with a comment stating the invariant, or have `RefreshPackPage` accept a trailing status override so the ordering dependency is explicit rather than positional.

comments.content:
Span is computed from note **tails** (`note.Nodes[^1].Time`) but buckets use note **head** time only. Two consequences:
1. A note's head can be far behind the tail that defines `span`, which is fine, but a note whose head lies beyond the last tail — i.e. a Hold whose tail is *earlier* than another note's tail, or any note past the max-tail position — is `Math.Clamp`-ed into the last bucket, piling an arbitrary number of notes into bucket 71 and skewing the density bar.
2. More importantly, `max` can only be 0 if `counts` is all zeros, which cannot happen once `chart.Notes.Count > 0` (every note increments exactly one bucket), so the division is safe — but this invariant is fragile and undocumented; a future early-`return`/skip inside the loop would silently produce NaN/∞.

Consider documenting the invariant or adding `if (max <= 0) return null;`, and clamping by `second >= span` explicitly with a note about tail-based span.

The cover cache key is only `root + relative` with no file metadata, so if the user replaces `cover.png` on disk with a new image under the same name (a normal authoring workflow), `RefreshPackPage` (e.g. after save or digest background completion) keeps returning the stale texture. The digest path already solves exactly this with `DigestAudioMetaKey` (last-write time + length); mirror that here, e.g. append `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc` + length to `key`. Also note that when decoding fails, `_packCoverKey` is still set to `key`, so a transient failure (file momentarily locked mid-save) is cached as "no cover" forever until path changes.

`MenuClicked` is invoked without first hiding the menu (unlike `_GuiInput`, which hides then invokes). The shell's `HandleMenu` runs synchronously and may call back into editor code (e.g. `ActSettings` → `OpenSettings`) while this Control is still visible with stale `_elements`. `headOnly` is meant to express "no body link" for a Hold's tail-drag ghost (see RefreshGameplayStage, which calls it with `tailStage`), but the parameter currently also drops the whole point list. For a Hold/Mixer the chain then renders as a single `HoldHead` note with `SubNoteId = -1`, i.e. a stub head with no body at all, which is not "head drawn with placed-entity appearance". The Mixer/other kinds corner is inconsistent too: a preview Mixer draft goes through the full path branch while a Hold draft does not. Please confirm the intended ghost appearance and make `headOnly` only suppress link/body rendering rather than the sample list.

The hit test mixes two time domains: the interval check uses authored display seconds (`note.Time` / `note.EndTime`), but the sample is taken at `SecondsToBar(seconds, CurrentBpms)`, which is the *current* tempo map conversion, and `PathShape(note)` carries the authored `TimeExact` values. After the BPM map changes (BPM event added/edited) the two can diverge, so the point sampled is not the point the user clicked on — body clicks silently miss or hit at the wrong width. `sample.Width` is also used unchanged for the slack comparison even though `place.Center` is clamped display-space geometry; prefer deriving the sample time from the same projection the click was resolved with (e.g. via `ExactTimeAt`/`BarAt`) instead of re-deriving bars from clamped seconds.

The new node inherits the curve of the enclosing interval and applies it to the *second half* of that interval. Rotating a curve mid-segment changes the shape: `Hold` / `EaseIn*` / `EaseOut*` / `Smooth` all have different starting and ending slopes, so the geometry after the insert point no longer matches the path the user sampled. Worse, when the enclosing interval is the last one, the tail node keeps its (tail-must-omit) curve and the inherited curve moves onto the new node — so the tail half is now shaped by a curve that previously did not exist there. The insert is documented as "shape zero-jump / values identical before and after", which is only true for `Linear`; consider either documenting/limiting this to a linear split, or re-fitting the curve on both halves.

comments.content: `onset` is derived from the quantized `progress`, so on frame 0 progress is 0 and onset is 0 → entire bloom (rings, rays, core) renders with alpha 0 for the first 1/12 of the lifetime. With a 0.36s lifetime that's a ~30ms dead frame followed by a hard pop at frame 1 (progress = 1/11 ≈ 0.09 → onset jumps from 0 to 1.0). The 0.08 divisor matches the first frame step exactly, so the onset ramp never actually has intermediate values. Use the raw (unquantized) progress for onset so the ramp is continuous across frame boundaries.

Bug: `outer` can be *smaller* than `inner` for some rays. For i=1 (odd): inner = 0.36r, (i+1)%3 = 2 → outer = 0.96r (ok). For i=3: inner = 0.36r, (3+1)%3 = 1 → outer = 0.84r. For i=5: (5+1)%3=0 → outer = 0.72r. For i=7: (7+1)%3=2 → 0.96r. So the ranges never invert here, but they do depend on the two independent moduli — a fragile, non-obvious pairing. More importantly the ray length varies discontinuously between 0.84r and 0.96r with no visible design intent. Consider a single explicit length table or a formula that guarantees `outer > inner` by construction.

With Intensity > 1 (settings allow up to 150%) radius/96 exceeds 1, the Lerp saturates at 86 and is then clamped by `halfSpan`; with Intensity < 1 the mine cross shrinks more than the rest of the effect relative to the radius. Also the magic constant 96 doesn't match the max radius 104. Normalize against the actual radius range and clamp the result, e.g. `Mathf.Clamp(rescaled, 30f, halfSpan)`.
